blocks.text: Documents the five routes, the three-way risk split (propose/write/go-live), and explains why these routes call agent modules directly rather than going through eo.registry. Also notes the W8.5 code-proposal review flow and why UptimeRobot needs HTTP routes while Sentry does not.
blocks.title: Module header and imports

blocks.text: Three small Pydantic models. DeployActionRequest carries just an optional project_unique_name. UptimeRobotKeyRequest carries an API key string. UptimeRobotRegisterRequest carries a URL and optional friendly name.
blocks.title: Request body models

blocks.text: deploy_propose calls deploy_config_writer then augments the plan dict with _file_plan_for_review's output. _file_plan_for_review returns {proposal: null, proposal_skipped: reason} when the plan is a fallback or the session has no workspace, otherwise creates a code proposal row for review and returns {proposal: {id, workspace_id, status, path}}.
blocks.title: Propose: LLM config generation and optional review filing

blocks.text: deploy_write writes the previously proposed config to disk — reversible and unconfirmed. deploy_go_live calls trigger_live_deploy, which blocks internally on a y/N confirmation. Both raise HTTPException(409) on MissingDependencyError, e.g. when no proposal exists.
blocks.title: Write and go-live

blocks.text: set_uptimerobot_key stores the key in workspace facts (409 if no workspace). register_uptimerobot immediately calls deploy_agent.register_uptimerobot_monitor, which contacts the UptimeRobot API for real. ValueError from the agent (bad URL, API error) becomes 400.
blocks.title: UptimeRobot monitoring endpoints

gotchas: deploy_write is the old unreviewed write path; workspace-backed projects in the Build tab no longer offer it
register_uptimerobot makes a real external API call with no confirmation gate — different risk class than deploy_go_live
MissingDependencyError from agent modules becomes a 409, not a 500
how_it_works: deploy_propose calls deploy_config_writer.run_deploy_config_writer, then optionally files the plan as a code proposal for review (W8.5) if the session belongs to a workspace
deploy_write calls deploy_agent.write_deploy_config to write the config file to disk — no confirmation required
deploy_go_live calls deploy_agent.trigger_live_deploy, which blocks on an interactive y/N confirmation inside the agent
set_uptimerobot_key stores the key in the workspace's facts dict via deploy_agent; register_uptimerobot makes an external API call immediately
outputs: plan dict plus proposal metadata on propose; deployment result on write/go-live; {status: saved} on key; monitor registration result
purpose: Exposes the HTTP surface for the deployment flow: proposing a config (LLM call, no write), writing the config file (reversible), and going live (interactive confirmation gate required). Also provides two monitoring endpoints for saving a UptimeRobot API key and registering a new URL monitor. Calls agent modules directly rather than through eo/executor.
side_effects: LLM call via deploy_config_writer on propose
external UptimeRobot API call on register_uptimerobot
code_proposals database write on propose when session has a workspace
summary: FastAPI router for deploy action buttons and UptimeRobot monitoring hooks; five POST endpoints, three distinct risk levels.
